decisions.reason: The particle-therapy water phantom is niche but strategically aligned with advanced radiotherapy QA and the firm's integrated workflow offering, so it is more likely to be retained than withdrawn.

This small-volume ionization chamber serves specialized dosimetry needs in the core measurement portfolio, though some portfolio rationalization risk remains after the earlier chamber-line withdrawal.

It still fits the firm's dosimetry business, but as another small-volume chamber in a potentially overlapping range it carries a somewhat elevated discontinuation risk versus more clearly differentiated products.
An ionization chamber for relative dosimetry supports routine clinical QA and complements the firm's service and software ecosystem, making continuation the more likely choice.
The thimble ionization chamber is a standard clinical instrument with stable demand, although competitive and overlap pressures make it somewhat more exposed than the most differentiated products.
